justification: Contributes an outer loop that iteratively rewrites the agent's own harness specification from its revision history; evidence is 30 synthetic lab tasks comparing reasoning-effort settings, not a deployed setting.
Abstract's claim is a co-evolving world model that sustains agent self-improvement on self-sampled trajectories; validated only on Mind2Web-Live, WebVoyager and GAIA-web benchmarks in the lab.

Contribution is a failure-driven self-improvement loop that diagnoses failed trajectories and emits code patches upgrading the agent; validated on the OSWorld benchmark with OpenCUA-72B, no real deployment.

Object is the confidence signal: it measures ECE drift under self-improvement and compares three calibration placements, a lab study of a judgement mechanism rather than practice; runner-up critique_and_revision.

Sweet&Sour changes how reflections are produced and fed back by adding positive experiences and managed memory; evaluated on text-game tasks across closed and open LLMs in the lab. Runner-up: memory_and_context_management.

Stated key innovation is perceptual validation, a vision-model check on rendered frames that judges generated simulation code; evidence is a prototype compared with single-shot baselines over seven self-chosen domains.
Self-evolving framework in which the agent recursively modifies its own logic and behaviour; claims rest on lab experiments on mathematical reasoning and agent tasks against manually crafted agents.
Agent iteratively progresses by identifying and learning from its own mistakes via structured self-reflection, i.e. the revision step; evidence is MiniWoB++ benchmark results against prior SoTA.
PreFlect's contribution is prospective reflection that criticises and refines plans before execution plus dynamic re-planning; evaluated on benchmarks against reflection baselines in the lab.

Concept of autoreflection: agents read and edit their own identity, memory and disposition files across activations; the paper argues a conceptual criterion set and illustrates it with three Moltbook agent case studies.
Formal Reflect mechanism detects prediction-observation mismatches and revises the agent's internal causal model; the abstract only lays theoretical groundwork, reporting no evaluation.

ASG-SI frames self-improvement as compiling successful trajectories into a growing auditable skill graph; the paper proposes an architecture, threat model and reference implementation demonstration rather than a validation study.
Formalises self-play self-improvement as a recursive Generator-Verifier-Updater flow and unifies STaR, SPIN and Reflexion under it; the contribution is theory and proofs, with no empirical study.

Argues introspection is the threshold condition for sustainable recursive self-improvement, a conceptual framework grounded in Kleene's recursion theorem plus a literature review, not a new technique or experiment.
Contributes CMP, a metric guiding the search over an agent's tree of self-modifications, i.e. the outer self-improvement loop; evidence is lab results on SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot.

Headline artefact is an evaluation protocol for judging long generation loops and what a judge can miss; evidence is 24 deliberately varied conditions with a pre-registered replication, run in the lab.
Self-evolving framework whose agent recursively rewrites its own logic and behaviour; supported by lab experiments across multiple domains against manually crafted agents (ACL 2025 long paper).
Agent-R is an iterative self-training loop that builds self-critique data from its own MCTS trajectories to retrain the agent; evidence is lab results in three interactive environments.
MARS synthesises principle and procedural reflections into rewritten instructions so the agent self-evolves between tasks; validated on six benchmarks against self-evolving baselines in the lab.

Contribution is the debate arrangement itself: several model instances propose and critique responses over rounds to converge; supported by lab accuracy and factuality gains on standard reasoning tasks.

Persistent object is a curated shared knowledge base written and distilled from task attempts while agents stay disposable; evidence is solve-rate and cost results on reasoning, coding and terminal benchmarks.
OPT-BENCH is an instrument for measuring iterative self-optimisation, 20 ML tasks plus 10 NP-hard problems; used to test 19 LLMs in the lab, no deployed setting.
Same benchmark instrument for measuring iterative self-optimisation loops across 20 ML tasks and 10 NP-hard problems; evidence is a lab sweep of 19 LLMs from 7 families.

ME-ICPO iteratively rewrites its response in context from self-assessed rewards, so the object is the revision step; claims backed by theory plus lab results on standard mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
HSI has an evolver and meta-evolver rewrite the agent's own harness across iterations from environment feedback; evidence is BALROG benchmark gains with a frozen backbone, a lab setting.
